decisive_items: an abnormal superior mesenteric artery–vein relationship, with the vein coursing to the left of the artery
The third portion of the duodenum was not seen in its expected location
an abnormally low transverse colon and right colic flexure, with small-bowel loops clustered above and to the right
response.rationale: The CT findings of SMA/SMV inversion, abnormal duodenal position, and low transverse colon/right colic flexure with right-sided small bowel are classic for intestinal malrotation. Acute pain and leukocytosis may reflect malrotation-related compromise, but the normal appendix and absence of ischemia argue against appendicitis and isolated volvulus.

rejected.why: Postprandial discomfort is nonspecific and there is no imaging evidence of bowel wall inflammation or chronic IBD.
Clustered loops and mesenteric congestion could suggest volvulus, but no ischemia and the specific malrotation signs are better explained by malrotation.
Clinical signs mimic appendicitis, but CT explicitly shows a normal appendix.
Clustered small-bowel loops are nonspecific; no hernia sac/defect is described and the SMA/SMV and duodenal findings point to malrotation.
